newsitem.title: CANADA: Parmalat bid for Ault expires July 3.
newsitem.headline: Parmalat bid for Ault expires July 3.

text.p: Italy's Parmalat Finanziaria SpA said on Thursday that its C$415 million offer for Canadian dairy foods maker Ault Foods Ltd would expire on July 3 at 2100 EDT/July 4 0100 GMT.
Parmalat also said in the details of its bid mailed to shareholders that the offer was conditional on 66-2/3 percent of shares being tendered.

Parmalat, Italy's largest listed food company, made its C$34 a share bid on Monday, topping a hostile C$28 a share offer by privately held Saputo Group Inc. Parmalat made the bid with its partner, U.S. bank Citicorp.
Parmalat added that it believed the Ault takeover would not pose a problem for Canada's Competition Bureau.
The bureau said this week that it would review the bid to see if it resulted in a substantial lessening of competition. In March Parmalt acquired a majority stake in Beatrice Foods for C$290 million.
Montreal-based Saputo has a 16.3 percent stake in Ault and has said it would not rule out a higher offer it it gained access to Ault's books.
Ault has three other major shareholders: Mackenzie Financial Corp at 17.2 percent, Caisse de depot et placement du Quebec at 16 percent and Sun Life Assurance Co of Canada with 14.7 percent.
Ault shares dipped 0.10 to 34.10 in light trading on Thursday on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
Parmalat shares closed 6.4 percent higher at 2,512 lire on the Milan equities exchange.
